commands.review_summary:
The PR changes the MCP loopback HTTP server to treat id-less JSON-RPC messages as notifications, return 202 empty bodies for notification-only paths, suppress normal notification responses, and add regression coverage.

PR surface: Source +25, Tests +77. Total +102 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: PR head still runs shared tool resolution before the per-message notification filter for mixed batches, and the catch serializes internal errors for every parsed batch entry. I did not run tests in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow mechanical repair can finish the mixed-batch notification contract, while the compatibility-visible behavior still needs owner acceptance before merge.

target.title: fix(gateway): MCP clients receive responses for JSON-RPC notifications
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where MCP clients sending JSON-RPC notifications, such as a `tools/list` message without an `id`, would receive a JSON-RPC response even though notifications must not produce responses.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MCP loopback HTTP server now detects JSON-RPC notifications by the absence of an own `id` property and suppresses responses for those messages. Notification-only `tools/list` requests return `202` with an empty body before scoped tool resolution, while side-effecting `tools/call` notifications still dispatch normally and only omit the response. Mixed batches that contain request messages still return responses for those request messages, while malformed entries and explicit `id: null` requests keep their existing response behavior.

## User Impact

MCP clients can send notification messages to the OpenClaw loopback MCP HTTP endpoint without seeing protocol-invalid response bodies or transient resolver errors on notification-only `tools/list` requests. Fire-and-forget `tools/call` notifications still execute, but do not receive a response body.

## Evidence

- RED regression proof before the original fix: the new notification test failed because the endpoint returned `200` instead of `202` for a `tools/list` notification without `id`.
- RED proof for the original pre-resolution failure path: a notification-only `tools/list` request with scoped tool resolution forced to throw returned `500` before the fast path was added.
- RED proof for the review finding: `notifications/initialized` and `notifications/cancelled` notification-only requests returned `500` instead of `202` when scoped tool resolution was forced to throw before the lifecycle notification fast path was added.
- RED proof for the side-effect regression guard: with an overly broad notification-only fast path restored locally, `tools/call` notifications returned `202` but did not resolve or execute the tool.
- Focused lifecycle notification proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts -t "does not resolve tools for notifications"`

  ```text
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  6 passed | 213 skipped (219)
  ```

- Direct raw POST transcript against `startMcpLoopbackServer` with the bearer token redacted:

  ```text
  === tools/list notification ===
  POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
  Host: 127.0.0.1:<loopback-port>
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted-owner-token>
  Content-Type: application/json

  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"tools/list"}
  HTTP 202
  response-body-bytes: 0
  response-body: <empty>
  === notifications/initialized notification ===
  POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
  Host: 127.0.0.1:<loopback-port>
  Authorization: Bearer <redacted-owner-token>
  Content-Type: application/json

  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"}
  HTTP 202
  response-body-bytes: 0
  response-body: <empty>
  ```

- Focused issue-specific runtime proof for `tools/list` notification-only requests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts -t "does not resolve tools for tools/list notification-only requests"`

  ```text
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  3 passed | 216 skipped (219)
  ```

- Focused regression proof for `tools/call` notification dispatch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts -t "dispatches tools/call notifications without returning a response"`

  ```text
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  3 passed | 216 skipped (219)
  ```

- MCP HTTP regression coverage: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts`

  ```text
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  219 passed (219)
  ```

- CI lint reproduction after the remote `check-lint` failure and after the round-two changes: `pnpm lint --threads=8`

  ```text
  [oxlint:core] finished
  [oxlint:extensions] finished
  [oxlint:scripts] finished
  ```

- OpenClaw dev gateway startup smoke completed from the PR worktree on the current HEAD with `http server listening` and `ready`; the issue-specific behavior proof above exercises the affected `startMcpLoopbackServer` HTTP path over real TCP requests.
- Boundary note: the pre-resolution path remains an allowlist for notification-only messages that do not need scoped tools; `tools/call` notifications still go through normal dispatch and only suppress the response body.
